Sampled candidate cross-entropy uses one positive plus 64 negative draws: L=logsumexp(s+,s−₁,…,s−₆₄)−s+. It learns competition within those 65 entries. Sampling-corrected softmax adjusts logits using sampling probabilities/expected counts; the correction must match replacement, uniqueness and target-inclusion rules. Subtracting the same log-q constant from all 65 logits cancels. By contrast, estimating an eligible-catalogue partition with an always-included target gives exp(s+)+(M/64)Σexp(s−), where M is the eligible negative count. These are different objectives; specify the convention. [TensorFlow derivation](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf)

gSASRec uses independent sigmoid terms, not candidate softmax: L=[β·softplus(−s+)+Σsoftplus(s−)]/65, with α=64/(|I|−1), β=1−t+tα. Thus t=0 gives ordinary BCE; increasing t reduces positive weighting to address sampling-induced overconfidence. Its official implementation transforms the positive logit before BCE; direct weighted softplus expresses the same loss stably. Changing eligibility changes the sampling assumptions, so catalogue-based calibration should not be silently treated as exact under user-specific exclusions. [Official implementation](https://github.com/asash/gsasrec)

Recommended sampler design: construct category-local eligible items excluding padding and the user’s complete training-positive set. Draw exactly 64 with replacement to permit duplicates; retain their multiplicity in either loss. For 64 unique negatives, sample without replacement and explicitly reject/skip cases with fewer than 64 eligible items; never silently shrink K. With replacement requires only one eligible item; zero requires an explicit skip/error. TensorFlow provides unique sampling and target-collision masking, not arbitrary per-user history exclusion. Build exclusions inside the dataset sampler while user identity is known, preserving the downstream `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` contract. Truncated sequences cannot reliably identify users or reconstruct complete exclusions. [Sampler documentation](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/random/uniform_candidate_sampler), [collision handling](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/nn/compute_accidental_hits)
